observation_summary: The @InjectMocks feature was incorrectly injecting mocks into fields when multiple candidates were available, because the filtering logic lacked sufficient context about other fields in the class.
reasoning_summary: The fix involved changing the method signature of 'filterCandidate' across multiple classes (FinalMockCandidateFilter, MockCandidateFilter, NameBasedCandidateFilter, TypeBasedCandidateFilter) to include the 'List<Field> fields' parameter. This change in the interface contract allowed the filtering logic to inspect other fields in the class to resolve naming conflicts, which is a classic boundary/contract mismatch issue between the injection mechanism and the candidate filtering components.
evidence_used: The fix modified the method signature of 'filterCandidate' in the 'MockCandidateFilter' interface and all its implementations.
The fix added 'List<Field> fields' to the method signature to provide necessary context for disambiguation.
The 'PropertyAndSetterInjection' class was updated to pass the 'orderedInstanceFields' list to the filter, confirming the change in the communication contract between the injector and the filter.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic inside the filter was updated, the primary mechanism of the fix was changing the interface contract (method signature) across multiple components to enable the new logic.
The fix addresses a communication contract mismatch between the injector and the filter, rather than a structural dependency or association constraint between data structures.
